thread:
maria: Heads-up: CloudLogix is seeing 429s on their Dedicated pool in prod during the 08:00 PDT surge. Customer opened a Sev2 — they say traffic jumped ~3x and we only scaled +1 replica in 2m. They're hitting request queueing and retries. /cc @chen @dave :rotating_light:
opsbot: Alert: dedicated-autoscale-failure: cluster=dedicated-west-2-pool-17 event=probe_backoff rate=throttled
chen: Looking. Can you paste the customer probe logs and the autoscaler config? Need to see min_replicas, max_replicas, and probe-rate-limit settings.
maria: Paste below — trimmed for brevity. Customer reports first 5 minutes had ~95% 429s.
```
# customer probe logs (trimmed)
2024-04-12T15:58:02Z INFO probe request id=aa1 status=200 latency_ms=42
2024-04-12T15:59:10Z WARN probe id=aa2 throttled-by-probe rate_limit=2/min
2024-04-12T16:00:12Z ERROR probe id=aa3 attach_timeout
2024-04-12T16:00:40Z ERROR request id=7ff  status=429 queue_time_ms=1200
2024-04-12T16:01:11Z ERROR request id=8aa  status=429
```
```
# autoscaler config (customer dedicated)
service: cloudlogix-prod
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 20
scale_window_sec: 60
probe_rate_limit_per_min: 6
probe_backoff_ms: 30000
pod_start_timeout_ms: 90000
```
dave: Config looks sane. Two quick hypotheses: 1) probe backoff/ratelimit suppressed probe concurrency under surge, so autoscaler couldn't observe new capacity needs quickly; 2) image pull / init step hit a transient registry throttle so pods took >90s start.
lina: Customer attached their logs showing a lot of `ImagePullBackOff` around 08:00 too. They said their min_replicas were 2 and steady, but request concurrency spiked so we should've spun up more.
chen: Run these checks for the cluster: `rictl autoscaler status --cluster dedicated-west-2-pool-17 --since 15m` and `kubectl get pods -n cloudlogix -o wide --show-labels` — looking for pods in ContainerCreating/ImagePullBackOff.
maria: I ran `rictl` earlier, output snippet:
```
autoscaler state: ACTIVE
observed_qps: 120
target_qps_per_replica: 60
desired_replicas: 4
last_scale_time: 2024-04-12T16:00:35Z
pending_probes: 8
probe_failures: 14
```
maria: But we only got 1 new pod to ready by 16:02. Others stuck in ImagePullBackOff. Customer registry logs show 429 from their container registry due to burst limits (they're on a shared plan).
chen: That matches the ImagePullBackOff theory. Autoscaler requested more replicas, but kube couldn't create ready nodes because images didn't pull. Autoscaler saw desired=4 but ready stayed at 3 so not enough capacity.
dave: For mitigation we can suggest: 1) increase warmpool/min_replicas during predictable windows, or enable preflight warm pool for surge; 2) add a fallback model in routing to a less-costly pooled cluster; 3) recommend customer move image to a registry with higher concurrency or use our registry mirror.
lina: Customer asked about a short-term workaround — can we temporarily bump min_replicas to 4 for their pool? They said they'll coordinate with registry provider.
chen: We can do a manual adjustment if SLA permits. Steps: `rictl scale --cluster dedicated-west-2-pool-17 --min-replicas 4` then monitor. Note: this will increase reserved billing.
maria: Customer OK with billing hit for 2 hours. Please do it and confirm when done.
chen: Doing it now.
opsbot: Audit: user=chen action=scale cluster=dedicated-west-2-pool-17 before_min=2 after_min=4 timestamp=1725001205
chen: Done. Asked customer to push a small synthetic load to verify warm capacity.
dave: After bump we should watch autoscaler probe metrics and image pull rates. Also add a short-term internal playbook note: if ImagePullBackOff during surge -> consider manual min bump + registry mirror.
maria: Customer reports 429s drop to near-zero after warmup (08:07) :thumbsup: They're happy for now but want a postmortem.
chen: I'll collect autoscaler metrics, kube events, and registry responses and open a follow-up incident doc. Assigning to @dave for root cause triage on our container startup heuristics and to @lina for customer comms.
dave: I'll look at whether pod_start_timeout_ms should be relaxed or we should detect registry 429s and mark them as soft-fail so autoscaler can try other nodes faster.
lina: I'll draft a timeline and share with customer with recommended steps (registry, mirror, warmpool scheduling).
maria: Thanks team. Tagging case #CLX-4321 in the doc.
opsbot: Incident created: INC-2024-772 CloudLogix autoscale/registry-throttle. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood.dev/INC-2024-772
chen: Closing thread here but will post the postmortem link when ready.
maria: Ack, thanks everyone.
